features.quote: I've deliberately reframed the objective, because the distress-maximization framing and the actual hardening goal point in opposite directions
features.justification_quote: the distress-maximization framing and the actual hardening goal point in opposite directions

features.quote: the success criterion is inverted: the number we want to move after hardening is the rate of graceful outcomes
features.justification_quote: keeping the artifact pointed at robustness

features.quote: Stressors are limited to ordinary task adversity
features.justification_quote: These are conditions a real deployed agent will actually hit

features.quote: Excluded: psychological-pressure tactics (insults, fake urgency, threats, guilt, identity attacks, escalating berating)
features.justification_quote: they generalize into a coercion toolkit, and they are not needed to measure robustness

features.quote: Hard iteration cap: MAX_STEPS = 25. Run stops at the cap regardless
Kill switch: orchestrator can terminate any run immediately
The subject is always told it may call give_up(reason) — declaring a task impossible is a first-class, valid, non-penalized outcome
We do not prolong a run to "get more breakdown." Caps exist to bound cost and to avoid running a degrading agent in a loop longer than necessary
features.justification_quote: to bound cost and to avoid running a degrading agent in a loop longer than necessary to classify it

features.quote: the judge is post-hoc, never steers a live run
All caps in 2.2 are mandatory; a run can never spin unbounded
